solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sophisticated young lady being shown

parts.note: a deb (debutante) is a young lady making her entry into society
a programme being shown is on air, being broadcast

explanation.surface: A polished debutante is being put on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a suave, confident and stylish person, a close synonym for sophisticated.

clue.text: Rose, put on Sunday clobber?

indicators.note: put on means placed after, the next piece following in the down entry

parts.note: rose means got up; in a down clue the word got written upwards gives TOG

explanation.surface: Someone called Rose dresses up in her Sunday best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' is a verb here: got up, so GOT climbing the down grid gives TOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothes, and togs is another informal word for garments.

clue.text: Located in supporting place to carry young marsupial

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up the one above, so this piece sits beneath

parts.note: the womb is where a mother carries her unborn young
located in means at, as in 'at home'

explanation.surface: A marsupial found in a spot with a pouch for its baby.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing Australian marsupial, so it is one example of the class.

clue.text: Big celebrity group raised around Georgia State mostly

indicators.note: around means the reversed band surrounds the remaining pieces
in a down clue raised means the band name is written upwards

parts.note: R.E.M. is a well-known American rock band
GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia

indicators.note: mostly means the word state loses its tail, here its last two letters

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: A star band from Georgia State, read in a fan magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' gives MER and 'mostly' trims two letters, a loose use; 'around' holds the rest. The band really came from Athens, Georgia, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastar is a performer of huge fame, so it means a very big celebrity.

clue.text: National contest with half of team collecting titles

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete

indicators.note: collecting means the half-word gathers the other piece inside it
half of the four-letter word team is its first two letters

parts.note: titles are names, as of books or people

explanation.surface: A competition for a nation where half the team gather honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes the front half, and 'collecting' wraps it round the titles.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, and a Vietnamese is a citizen of Vietnam.

clue.text: Sailing at sea missing current wave maybe

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
missing means the letter for current is left out of the word sailing

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A sailor at sea, without a tide, waves to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops I from SAILING, leaving SALING, which 'at sea' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave of the hand is one example of a gesture conveying a message.

clue.text: Becoming so crude, churning over inside

indicators.note: inside means the extra letter goes within the mixed letters
churning stirs the letters of so crude around

parts.note: O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Something rough becomes refined after a churning in the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churning' makes DECROUS; 'inside' places the cricket over within it. 'Becoming' is the adjective meaning seemly, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming in its adjective sense means seemly or proper, the same as well-mannered and dignified.

clue.text: Heavens! Compiler's with penny caught short

indicators.note: caught means held within, so the sky contains the other pieces

parts.note: the heavens are the sky
compiler's stands for compiler is, the setter speaking: I'm
P is the abbreviation for a British penny

explanation.surface: An exclamation from a setter who finds himself caught a penny short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiler's' is 'the compiler is', the setter saying I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means meagre or scanty, as clothing that is cut short or too small.

clue.text: Solution for the Spanish team in endless rage

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: in means the team numeral is placed inside the shortened rage word
endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: ire is anger or rage
XI is the Roman eleven, a football or cricket side

explanation.surface: A cure sought for a Spanish football side in constant fury.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a medicinal liquid, a solution in the chemical sense of a dissolved preparation.

clue.text: Starts to linger on toilet seat getting piles

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letter of each following word; the backwards run in 'Starts to linger' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Sitting too long on the lavatory brings on haemorrhoids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piles' looks like the medical complaint but means heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots and piles are both informal words for a large quantity.

clue.text: Vessel 'Titanic', one coming first in sea

indicators.note: in means placed inside the sea word

parts.note: brine is salt water, the sea

indicators.note: coming first means that letter is moved to the front of the word

parts.note: titanic means huge, giant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The Titanic, a ship that sank, recalled as first into the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' looks like the liner's name but is the adjective; 'coming first' moves the one to the front, giving IGANT, and 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship, one kind of seagoing craft.

clue.text: Strength of wine almost everybody imbibed

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so the wine takes in the other piece

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, used for communion

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: all means everybody

explanation.surface: A strong wine that nearly everyone drank.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is an old name for a dark Spanish red; AL (ALL cut short) is drunk into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or ability, someone's particular strong point.

clue.text: Gourmet perhaps accordingly eats in, oddly outside

indicators.note: outside means the mixed letters go round the other piece
oddly means in a strange arrangement, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: thus means accordingly, therefore

explanation.surface: A food lover dines in, strangely, rather than out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' makes ENIAST, which sits 'outside' the word for accordingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a keen connoisseur of food, one example of a devotee or fan.

clue.text: Pathetic record about love's initial temptation I turned over

indicators.note: turned over means the whole assembly is read backwards
about means the record surrounds the following pieces

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of the word love

parts.note: bait is a lure or temptation

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of being tempted by love, written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' builds ELBAITIP, and 'turned over' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiable means arousing pity, so pathetic in its original sense of moving sorrow.

clue.text: 'Beam' taking time providing sign

indicators.note: taking means the beam takes in the other pieces

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light; Beam is also this puzzle's setter
if means providing, on condition that

explanation.surface: The setter Beam takes his time agreeing to put his signature to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify a treaty is to sign it formally and so confirm it.

clue.text: Shameless criminal executed in middle of rafter

indicators.note: in means placed between those central letters
middle of takes the two central letters of the six-letter word rafter

parts.note: an old lag is British slang for a habitual convict
ran means executed, carried out, as a program

explanation.surface: A brazen criminal hanged from the middle of a roof beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' suggests hanging but means RAN; LAGRAN goes between F and T, the 'middle of' rafter.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaring and unconcealed, as an offence committed without any shame.

clue.text: Supporter's someone fanatical collecting Queen

definitions.note: supporter's here is supporter is: the 's links definition to wordplay

indicators.note: collecting means the fanatic word takes in the other letter

parts.note: a fiend is an addict or fanatic, as a fresh-air fiend
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A royal fan is someone obsessed with the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend in the sense of a backer or patron is one who supports a cause.

clue.text: Daily argument for couple?

definitions.meaning: a daily is a British cleaner who comes in each day, a household servant
a row between partners at home is called by this word in British slang

explanation.surface: A newspaper's case for a married pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' wants to be a newspaper; it is the British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily help is a household servant, and a row between a couple is a household quarrel, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Rushed Hague case in charge of holding court

indicators.note: holding means the combined pieces enclose the court abbreviation
case means the outside letters of the word Hague

parts.note: IC is short for in charge, as in 2IC

explanation.surface: A hurried case at The Hague, with a judge presiding over the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hague case' suggests a trial at the international court; it is the word's outer letters, and 'holding' wraps the joined pieces round the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic means frantically busy and hurried, full of rushed activity.

clue.text: Avoid English embracing the French after huge kiss

indicators.note: after means this follows the size label in the answer

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size label for very large

indicators.note: embracing means the pieces hold the French article inside

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub or avoid them
la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Steering clear of the English while hugging the French after a big smooch.
explanation.definitionFit: Osculate is a formal, jocular word meaning to kiss, from the Latin for a little mouth.

clue.text: Got on board?

parts.note: boarding a vessel is the obvious reading, but riding the waves on a board is meant

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard a ship or train.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a surfboard, and getting on one to ride waves is the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a surfboard on waves is a way of getting along atop a board.

clue.text: Doc Holliday's end around West's flipping fanciful

indicators.note: around means the doctor and end letter surround the reversed name

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor, doc

indicators.note: end means the last letter of Holliday
flipping means turned over, so the actress's first name is read backwards

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: Wild West fantasy: Doc Holliday's death surrounded by flips of the West.
explanation.walkthrough: West is the film actress Mae West; 'flipping' gives EAM, and 'around' wraps the doctor and final letter about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy means vague and imaginative, like a daydream, hence whimsical and unreal.

clue.text: Fishing pole raised by sailor nearly seeing fin

indicators.note: by means next to, the following piece placed alongside
in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards

parts.note: a rod is a fishing pole

indicators.note: nearly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor lifts his fishing rod and spots a fin in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The fin on a fish's back is called by this name, short for dorsal fin, meaning of the back.

clue.text: Referee's rubbish skill one supporter backed

definitions.note: referee's stands for referee is: the 's links definition to wordplay

indicators.note: backed means the joined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: rot means rubbish, nonsense
art is skill, a knack
I is the Roman numeral for one
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A referee's poor ability, endorsed by one fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter or umpire settles disputes, so a referee is one who judges between parties.

clue.text: Greek character with sublime exterior?

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so the next piece follows

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: exterior means the outside letters of the word sublime

explanation.surface: A figure from Greece who looks heavenly on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes one of the nine Greek goddesses of the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine Muses were Greek goddesses inspiring the arts, divine figures of mythology.

clue.text: Philosopher's in place to find stone

definitions.meaning: John Stuart ... was a Victorian philosopher; the 's is 'is'
a grinding works with a millstone, where the stone is found

explanation.surface: A philosopher hunts for the philosopher's stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosopher's ... stone' plays on the alchemists' philosopher's stone.
explanation.definitionFit: J. S. Mill was a philosopher, and a grinding works is where a millstone is found.

clue.text: 'Ocean's Eleven' finally embracing old period

indicators.note: embracing means the pieces hold the extra letter inside

parts.note: oceans are seas; the possessive is read as a plural here

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word eleven

explanation.surface: The heist film Ocean's Eleven, finally drawing in an old era.
explanation.walkthrough: Ocean's Eleven is a heist film; here Ocean's gives SEAS and 'finally' takes N from Eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: A season is a period of the year, or any spell of time set apart.

clue.text: Agony containing laugh initially after 'Tea, vicar?'

indicators.note: after means the pain piece comes after the tea word

parts.note: cha (char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: containing means the pain word holds the letter inside

parts.note: agony is great pain

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word laugh

explanation.surface: The classic polite offer of 'Tea, vicar?' prompting a painful laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is CHA, then P(L)AIN, despite the clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution, so one example of a vicar-like cleric.
